deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no derivation. It is a heavily corrected draft of a covering letter, almost certainly to C. W. Borchardt as editor of Crelle's Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik. It accompanies the manuscript of 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (J. reine angew. Math. 54, 1857). The page is folio 149r of the bundle R.AbelTheta, and the letter is written on a printed customs or freight form whose columns read No. der Karte, Zeichen, Stück, Pfund, Loth.

Content, in order:
(1) 'Hochgeehrter Herr Doctor': Riemann sends the announced treatise on Abelian functions and asks for its speedy acceptance into the Journal.
(2) He apologises that finishing the treatise took longer than expected. This also delayed his answer to the editor's letter 'vom 24. v. M.' (of the 24th of last month).
(3) He addresses the editor's offer to print 'meine drei kleinen Abhandlungen' and a proposed reprint of his Inaugural-Dissertation (Göttingen 1851) with minor changes. Together with the next page, his position appears to be this: the dissertation has become largely dispensable because the small papers contain its essential material. These are presumably the three preliminary notes printed in Crelle 54 ahead of the main memoir:
  - 'Allgemeine Voraussetzungen und Hülfsmittel für die Untersuchung von Functionen unbeschränkt veränderlicher Grössen';
  - 'Lehrsätze aus der analysis situs für die Theorie der Integrale von zweigliedrigen vollständigen Differentialien';
  - 'Bestimmung einer Function einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse durch Grenz- und Unstetigkeitsbedingungen'.
(4) Separately headed 'in der Dissert.', he quotes the dissertation's topological lemma for correction or comment: 'dass eine n+1fach zusammenhängende Fläche durch jeden sie nicht zerstückelnden Querschnitt in eine nfach zusammenhängende verwandelt wird' ('an (n+1)-fold connected surface is turned into an n-fold connected one by every cross-cut that does not dissect it'). He adds 'und andere hieraus gezogene Folgerungen' (and other consequences drawn from it), followed by a note on adapting this to the present circumstances.

In modern terms, the lemma says the following. Let F be a compact bordered surface with Riemann connectivity N = 2 - χ(F) for connected F (i.e. first Betti number + 1). A cross-cut is a simple arc joining two boundary points. A non-separating cross-cut lowers N by 1, since χ rises by 1. In the Analysis-situs note of 1857 Riemann reformulates this more carefully, including the separating case, where the sum over components of (N_i - 1) drops by 1.
(5) The last line probably says he has marked some (misprints or) notes in the enclosed little booklet, presumably a copy of the dissertation.

No mathematical computation is performed on this page. The editorial context is the publication history of the 1857 Abelian-functions memoir and the relation between its preparatory notes and the 1851 dissertation.
errors: No mathematical errors on the page. The quoted dissertation lemma is correct as stated for non-separating cross-cuts. Riemann's apparent wish to qualify its 'consequences' matches the more careful treatment in the 1857 Analysis-situs note, which also covers cross-cuts that dissect the surface.

results.what: A non-separating cross-cut reduces the connectivity of a surface from n+1 to n (quoted from the 1851 dissertation)
results.modern_name: Effect of cutting along a non-separating arc on the Euler characteristic / first Betti number (connectivity of bordered surfaces)

results.what: Editorial correspondence: the Abelian functions memoir sent to the Crelle editor, the decision on a dissertation reprint, and the three preliminary notes
results.modern_name: Publication history of 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (1857)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft cover letter to the journal editor about publishing the 1857 memoir and handling the dissertation. Its only mathematical content is a quotation of Riemann's own well-known connectivity lemma. It is of minor biographical and editorial interest only.

checkable.asserts: A closed genus-p surface with one boundary hole has Riemann connectivity N = 2 - χ = 2p+1.
A non-separating cross-cut raises χ by 1 and so lowers connectivity N = 2-χ by exactly 1 (n+1 -> n).
2p cross-cuts reduce the (2p+1)-fold connected surface T' of a genus-p Riemann surface to a simply connected one.

transcription_corrections: Final line: 'einige Zeichen vorgezeichnet' more plausibly reads 'einige Druckfehler angezeichnet' (marked some misprints in the enclosed booklet).

'über die Hypergeometrische Reihe' is doubtful. Given the next page ('durch diese drei kleinen Abhandlungen entbehrlich geworden'), the struck-through passage more likely says the dissertation has been made dispensable by the small papers. A reference to the hypergeometric-series paper is unlikely.
'Gegen einen Wiederabdruck meiner Inaug. Diss. mit unbedeutenden Abänderungen' is a likely reading of the struck lines.

The quotation reads 'n+1fach zusammenhängende Fläche durch jeden sie nicht zerstückelnden Querschnitt in eine nfach zusammenhängende verwandelt wird'. It is headed 'in der Dissert.', i.e. a passage of the dissertation, not of the new memoir.
The addressee 'Herr Doctor' is presumably Borchardt (Crelle's Journal). The 'drei kleinen Abhandlungen' are the preliminary notes of Crelle vol. 54.
